questions: Creatinine is more reliable than urea as a GFR marker because filtered urea is partly *reabsorbed:What happens to filtered urea when tubular flow is slow?* in the tubule and its production varies with diet and catabolism.
When the BUN-to-creatinine ratio exceeds 20, the pattern suggests *pre-renal/prerenal:Is the kidney itself damaged, or is it underperfused?* azotaemia from dehydration, haemorrhage or heart failure.

In pre-renal azotaemia the urine is *concentrated:A healthy kidney receiving less blood tries to hold on to water.* and the fractional excretion of sodium is below 1 percent, supporting sodium and water conservation by the nephron.
Nephrotic syndrome is defined by proteinuria exceeding *3.5:Below this threshold is non-nephrotic proteinuria.* grams per day together with hypoalbuminaemia, oedema and hyperlipidaemia.

overallFeedback.feedback: These values form the framework for renal report interpretation: urea's variable reabsorption explains why creatinine is preferred; a BUN-to-creatinine ratio above 20 can support pre-renal azotaemia; concentrated urine and a FENa below 1% support sodium and water conservation but do not independently confirm the diagnosis — interpret alongside clinical findings, medicines and any kidney disease; and the 3.5 g/day threshold defines nephrotic-range proteinuria.
